description: Comprehensive signal taxonomy for {{COMPANY}} outbound engine. Inspired by ColdIQ 137-trigger framework + gtm-starter-kit signal decay patterns.

categories.name: Regulatory & Financial Filings
categories.description: Public disclosures where companies explicitly acknowledge AI/cybersecurity risk. Highest-confidence signals because they are legally attested.

signals.name: 10-K AI/Cybersecurity Risk Factor
signals.description: Annual SEC filing Risk Factors or MD&A section explicitly discusses AI/GenAI adoption and/or cybersecurity/data-security/regulatory risk.
signals.detection_method: SEC EDGAR full-text search on most recent 10-K
signals.sample_hook: Your 2025 10-K called out AI governance as a material risk. Most companies flagging that are 6-12 months from a compliance gap.

signals.name: 10-Q Quarterly AI/Security Update
signals.description: Quarterly filing references new AI initiatives, security incidents, or governance program updates.
signals.detection_method: SEC EDGAR full-text search on most recent 10-Q
signals.sample_hook: Your latest quarterly filing mentioned expanding AI capabilities. Are you scaling governance at the same speed?

signals.name: EU AI Act Compliance Disclosure
signals.description: Company publicly discusses EU AI Act compliance preparations, high-risk AI system classification, or conformity assessments.
signals.detection_method: Press release search + annual report keyword scan
signals.sample_hook: You disclosed EU AI Act prep in your latest report. Most companies at your stage are finding the conformity assessment requirements more complex than expected.

signals.name: OCC MRA/MRIA on Technology Risk
signals.description: OCC examination results in a Matter Requiring Attention (MRA) or Matter Requiring Immediate Attention (MRIA) related to technology, model risk, or cybersecurity.
signals.detection_method: OCC enforcement actions database + company disclosure
signals.sample_hook: Regulatory findings on technology risk create urgency. Companies in your position typically need a governance framework in place within 12 months.

signals.name: SOX Internal Controls - AI Mention
signals.description: Company's SOX 404 disclosure or internal controls narrative references AI/ML systems in scope of controls testing.
signals.detection_method: Proxy statement and 10-K internal controls section
signals.sample_hook: When AI models are in scope for SOX controls, audit teams need a governance trail that doesn't exist in most orgs yet.

signals.name: FDIC/Fed Consent Order - Technology Related
signals.description: Bank receives a consent order from FDIC, Federal Reserve, or state regulator related to technology risk management, BSA/AML, or cybersecurity.
signals.detection_method: FDIC enforcement actions database
signals.sample_hook: Consent orders on technology risk typically require demonstrable progress within 180 days. Governance infrastructure that satisfies examiners is what we do.

signals.name: State Privacy Law Applicability
signals.description: Company headquartered in or doing significant business in a state with a new or amended privacy/AI law (CCPA/CPRA, Colorado AI Act, etc.).
signals.detection_method: Company HQ + ops footprint vs. state AI/privacy law database
signals.sample_hook: The Colorado AI Act goes into effect next year. Companies deploying high-risk AI systems need documented governance before enforcement starts.

signals.name: Proxy Statement - Board AI Discussion
signals.description: Company's proxy statement or corporate governance filing mentions AI oversight at the board level, new AI committee, or board member with AI expertise.
signals.detection_method: SEC EDGAR proxy statement (DEF 14A) keyword scan
signals.sample_hook: Board-level AI oversight usually means the governance question is coming from the top. The next question is: what infrastructure makes that oversight possible?

signals.name: Earnings Call AI Strategy Discussion
signals.description: CEO/CFO discusses AI strategy, investment, or challenges during quarterly earnings call.
signals.detection_method: Earnings transcript keyword search (Seeking Alpha, company IR)
signals.sample_hook: Your CEO flagged AI as a priority on the last earnings call. In our experience, that executive commitment typically outpaces the governance infrastructure by 6+ months.

categories.name: AI Investment & Initiatives
categories.description: Concrete commitments to AI adoption. Companies spending money on AI need governance before or shortly after deployment.

signals.name: Stated AI Investment/Budget
signals.description: Company publicly announces a specific dollar amount or multi-year budget for AI/GenAI initiatives.
signals.detection_method: Press release, earnings call transcript, or investor deck
signals.sample_hook: You announced a $X investment in AI. In our experience, companies scaling that fast typically discover the governance gap 3-6 months in.

signals.name: Enterprise GenAI Rollout
signals.description: Company-wide deployment of GenAI tools (Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, Claude for Business, etc.) announced or detected.
signals.detection_method: Press release, vendor partnership announcement, job postings
signals.sample_hook: Rolling out GenAI enterprise-wide is the easy part. The hard part: knowing which 50 AI agents are running that your CISO doesn't know about yet.

signals.name: Flagship AI Vendor Partnership
signals.description: Company announces strategic partnership with a major AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Google, AWS Bedrock, Databricks, etc.).
signals.detection_method: Press release, partner directory, vendor case study
signals.sample_hook: Partnering with [vendor] to build on their models is smart. The next question most CISOs ask: how do I govern access to 26 models under one policy?

signals.name: AI Center of Excellence Launch
signals.description: Company establishes an AI Center of Excellence, AI lab, or dedicated AI business unit.
signals.detection_method: Press release, LinkedIn company page, job postings for CoE roles
signals.sample_hook: Standing up an AI CoE is step one. Step two is making sure every model that comes out of it has an audit trail before it hits production.

signals.name: Responsible AI / AI Ethics Program
signals.description: Company launches or announces a responsible AI, AI ethics, or AI governance program.
signals.detection_method: Press release, careers page, published AI principles doc
signals.sample_hook: Publishing AI principles is step one. Step two is tooling that enforces them. Most responsible AI programs stall between the policy and the enforcement layer.

signals.name: AI/ML Patent Filing
signals.description: Company files patents related to AI/ML applications, indicating active R&D and potential production deployment.
signals.detection_method: USPTO patent search, Google Patents
signals.sample_hook: You're actively patenting AI applications. Companies at that stage typically have more models in development than their governance infrastructure can track.

signals.name: AI Company Acquisition
signals.description: Company acquires an AI/ML startup or division, signaling accelerated AI capability buildout.
signals.detection_method: Press release, M&A database (Crunchbase, PitchBook)
signals.sample_hook: Acquiring [target] brings new AI models into your environment overnight. The governance question: can your existing controls see and manage what you just bought?

signals.name: Internal AI Hackathon / Innovation Sprint
signals.description: Company hosts or participates in an AI hackathon, innovation sprint, or AI challenge, indicating grassroots AI adoption.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn posts, company blog, Devpost
signals.sample_hook: Hackathons produce great AI prototypes. They also produce shadow AI that nobody governs when the prototype becomes a production tool.

signals.name: Cloud AI/ML Spend Increase
signals.description: Company's cloud spending on AI/ML services (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure AI) shows significant increase based on public disclosures or job postings.
signals.detection_method: Earnings call references to cloud AI spend, FinOps job postings
signals.sample_hook: Scaling cloud AI spend usually means models are moving from experiments to production. That's exactly when governance becomes non-optional.

categories.name: Leadership Changes
categories.description: New leaders make decisions fast. A new CISO, CDO, or CAO typically has a 90-day window to set priorities.

signals.name: New CISO Appointed
signals.description: Company appoints a new Chief Information Security Officer, often bringing new priorities and vendor evaluations.
signals.detection_method: Company press release, LinkedIn profile change, news search
signals.sample_hook: New CISOs typically audit their AI security posture in the first 90 days. The question is whether they find the governance layer or the gaps first.

signals.name: New Chief AI/Data Officer Appointed
signals.description: Company creates or fills a Chief AI Officer, Chief Data Officer, or Chief Analytics Officer role.
signals.detection_method: Company press release, LinkedIn
signals.sample_hook: A new CAO's first 90 days usually reveals how many AI models are running without governance. That's where the conversation starts.

signals.name: CISO Departure / Transition
signals.description: Current CISO announces departure, creating a leadership gap and potential for new vendor evaluations when successor arrives.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn profile change, press release, news
signals.sample_hook: CISO transitions create a window. The incoming leader will re-evaluate the security stack. Being in the conversation early matters.

signals.name: Board-Level AI Committee Formed
signals.description: Company forms a board-level committee or subcommittee specifically for AI oversight and governance.
signals.detection_method: Proxy statement, press release, board governance page
signals.sample_hook: Board-level AI oversight means governance pressure is coming from the top. The question: what does the reporting infrastructure look like?

signals.name: New CTO/CIO Appointed
signals.description: New technology leadership often brings a 90-day technology stack review and new vendor evaluations.
signals.detection_method: Company press release, LinkedIn
signals.sample_hook: New tech leaders typically review the full stack in the first quarter. AI governance is usually the biggest gap they find.

signals.name: VP of AI/ML Hired
signals.description: Company hires a VP-level leader specifically for AI/ML, indicating scaled investment and need for governance infrastructure.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn, press release, job posting
signals.sample_hook: Bringing in VP-level AI leadership usually means the company is past experimentation. Governance infrastructure becomes table stakes.

signals.name: Head of AI Risk / Model Risk Hired
signals.description: Company creates and fills a dedicated AI risk or model risk management leadership role.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn, job posting filled notification
signals.sample_hook: Hiring for AI risk means you've acknowledged the problem. The next step: tooling that gives that person visibility across every model.

signals.name: CISO Gains Board Observer Seat
signals.description: Proxy or governance update elevates the CISO/CAO to a board observer role with explicit AI oversight responsibilities.
signals.detection_method: Proxy statements, investor relations governance updates, board committee charters
signals.sample_hook: When the CISO gains a board seat they need dashboards that prove AI controls are real—here's how peers deliver that evidence.

categories.name: Hiring Patterns
categories.description: Job postings reveal future plans. Hiring for AI governance, model risk, or security roles indicates governance is becoming a priority.

signals.name: AI Governance Role Posted
signals.description: Open job posting for AI governance, responsible AI, or AI policy roles.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: You're hiring for AI governance. Before that person even starts, we can have the infrastructure in place for them to govern.

signals.name: Model Risk Manager/Analyst Posted
signals.description: Open posting for model risk management roles, indicating SR 11-7 or similar compliance needs extending to AI models.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: Model risk management is evolving from traditional quant models to LLMs. The validation requirements are different. Your MRM team will need tooling built for AI models.

signals.name: AI Security / ML Security Role Posted
signals.description: Open posting specifically for AI security, ML security, or AI red team roles.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: Hiring AI security talent is smart. Giving them a platform that covers 26 models on day one is smarter.

signals.name: MLOps/AI Platform Engineering Hiring Surge
signals.description: Company posts 3+ MLOps, AI platform engineering, or ML infrastructure roles within 30 days, indicating scale-up.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs aggregate, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: Hiring 3+ MLOps engineers means AI is going from experiment to production. That's exactly when governance moves from nice-to-have to critical.

signals.name: Data Protection Officer Posting
signals.description: Company hiring or newly designating a DPO, often indicating GDPR/privacy compliance work that intersects with AI governance.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: DPOs increasingly need visibility into AI data processing. If your AI models touch personal data, governance isn't optional.

signals.name: Prompt Engineer / AI Engineer Hiring
signals.description: Company hiring prompt engineers or AI application engineers, indicating active LLM deployment.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: Prompt engineers build AI agents. Who governs what those agents can access and do? That's the gap we close.

signals.name: AI Compliance / Regulatory Analyst Posting
signals.description: Posting for roles focused on AI regulatory compliance (EU AI Act, state AI laws, sector-specific AI regulations).
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: AI compliance hires need something to comply against. The platform that gives them real-time visibility is what separates audit-ready from audit-scramble.

signals.name: SOC Team Expansion (3+ Roles)
signals.description: Company expands SOC team significantly, indicating security operations investment that may extend to AI security monitoring.
signals.detection_method: LinkedIn Jobs aggregate, company careers page
signals.sample_hook: Expanding your SOC team is the right move. Are they equipped to monitor AI agent activity alongside traditional security events?

categories.name: Technology Shifts
categories.description: Platform changes and vendor transitions create natural buying windows for new tooling.

signals.name: Major Cloud Migration
signals.description: Company announces or is mid-execution of a major cloud migration (on-prem to cloud, or cloud-to-cloud), creating the infrastructure foundation for AI adoption.
signals.detection_method: Press release, cloud partner announcements, job postings for cloud roles
signals.sample_hook: Cloud migrations unlock AI at scale. But they also move the governance perimeter. If your AI governance plan is built for on-prem, it's already outdated.

signals.name: LLM Vendor Adoption Announcement
signals.description: Company announces adoption of a specific LLM vendor (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) for enterprise use.
signals.detection_method: Press release, vendor case study, technology partner page
signals.sample_hook: Adopting [vendor] is step one. What happens when you need a second model for a different use case? Single-vendor lock-in is the governance trap most companies don't see coming.

signals.name: Multi-Model / Multi-LLM Strategy
signals.description: Company publicly discusses or implements a multi-model AI strategy, using different LLMs for different use cases.
signals.detection_method: Press release, conference talk, job postings mentioning multi-model
signals.sample_hook: Multi-model is the right strategy. The hard part: unified governance across 5+ models from different vendors. One platform, one policy layer, every model covered.

signals.name: Data Platform Modernization
signals.description: Company invests in modern data stack (Snowflake, Databricks, data mesh, etc.), creating the data foundation for AI workloads.
signals.detection_method: Press release, vendor partnership, technology blog posts
signals.sample_hook: Modern data platforms make AI possible. They also make data governance more complex. When your AI models can access everything, who decides what they should access?

signals.name: Security Stack Overhaul / SIEM Migration
signals.description: Company migrating SIEM, SOAR, or core security tools, creating a natural buying window for adjacent AI security tooling.
signals.detection_method: Job postings mentioning tool migration, vendor switch announcements
signals.sample_hook: Migrating your security stack is the right time to ask: does the new architecture cover AI agent activity? Most SIEM deployments don't.

signals.name: Zero Trust Architecture Implementation
signals.description: Company implementing zero trust architecture, indicating mature security posture and potential extension to AI workloads.
signals.detection_method: Press release, CISO blog post, vendor partnership announcement
signals.sample_hook: Zero trust for networks is done. Zero trust for AI agents is next. Can you verify every model call the same way you verify every network request?

signals.name: Kubernetes / AI Infrastructure Deployment
signals.description: Company deploying K8s-based AI/ML infrastructure (KubeFlow, Ray, vLLM clusters), indicating production-scale AI workloads.
signals.detection_method: Job postings, GitHub org activity, conference talks
signals.sample_hook: Running AI inference at scale on Kubernetes. The operational maturity is there. The governance maturity usually isn't.

signals.name: AI API Gateway / AI Proxy Implementation
signals.description: Company implementing an AI proxy, gateway, or access control layer for LLM API calls.
signals.detection_method: Job postings, engineering blog, conference talks
signals.sample_hook: Building an AI gateway in-house is a 6-month project. Or you can deploy one that covers 26 models with unified governance in two weeks.

categories.name: Competitive Movement
categories.description: Vendor evaluations, contract renewals, and competitor frustration create displacement opportunities.

signals.name: Active Vendor Evaluation / RFP
signals.description: Company is actively evaluating AI governance, AI security, or related tooling through a formal RFP or vendor selection process.
signals.detection_method: RFP databases, procurement portals, intent data (Bombora/G2)
signals.sample_hook: If you're evaluating AI governance platforms, we'd rather be in the conversation early than not at all. Two-week POC, no commitment.

signals.name: G2 Comparison / Category Research
signals.description: Company employees viewing G2 comparison pages for AI governance, AI security, or related categories.
signals.detection_method: G2 buyer intent data, intent data providers
signals.sample_hook: Looks like your team is researching AI governance tools. Happy to save you time: here's what we do differently in 2 sentences.

signals.name: Incumbent Vendor Contract Expiry
signals.description: Known contract renewal window for current security or AI tooling vendor, creating evaluation opportunity.
signals.detection_method: Procurement records, FOIA for public sector, vendor contract databases
signals.sample_hook: Contract renewals are the right time to ask whether your current tools can handle AI governance. If not, adding a governance layer doesn't require ripping anything out.

signals.name: Negative Review of Current AI/Security Vendor
signals.description: Employee or company leaves a negative review of their current AI platform or security vendor on G2, Gartner Peer Insights, or TrustRadius.
signals.detection_method: G2, Gartner Peer Insights, TrustRadius review monitoring
signals.sample_hook: Vendor frustration is a signal. If your current platform can't cover multi-model AI governance, it's worth a 15-minute conversation.

signals.name: Competitor Customer Churning
signals.description: Company known to use a competitor's product shows signs of churning (layoffs at competitor, product deprecation, pricing increases).
signals.detection_method: Competitor news, pricing change announcements, layoff trackers
signals.sample_hook: If your current AI governance vendor is going through changes, it might be worth seeing what stable infrastructure looks like.

signals.name: Visited Competitor Booth at Conference
signals.description: Company representative scanned badge or visited competitor booth at an industry conference.
signals.detection_method: Conference attendee data, badge scan analytics
signals.sample_hook: You were checking out AI governance solutions at [conference]. Worth a 10-minute call to see how our approach differs.

signals.name: Governance Bakeoff Downselect
signals.description: Procurement down-selects AI governance vendors to a final bakeoff and circulates evaluation calendars internally.
signals.detection_method: Procurement portal status updates, FOIA disclosures, systems integrator intel
signals.sample_hook: If you're already in a governance bakeoff, we can deliver the control reports evaluators score highest—happy to share the template.

signals.name: Peer Reference Request
signals.description: Prospect asks existing customers or partners for references about AI governance platforms, signaling late-stage evaluation.
signals.detection_method: Partner/channel notifications, G2 inquiry alerts, customer reference desk workflows
signals.sample_hook: If you're collecting references, we can facilitate a call with a customer who replaced your incumbent in under 45 days.

categories.name: Corporate Events
categories.description: Major corporate transitions create new budgets, new priorities, and new vendor evaluation windows.

signals.name: M&A Announcement
signals.description: Company announces acquisition of or merger with another company, creating integration challenges and expanded AI governance scope.
signals.detection_method: SEC filing (8-K), press release, M&A databases
signals.sample_hook: Acquisitions bring new AI models, new data, and new governance gaps into your environment overnight. Unified governance across both entities is the fast path.

signals.name: IPO Filing / S-1
signals.description: Company files S-1 or announces IPO, creating compliance pressure and investor scrutiny on AI governance.
signals.detection_method: SEC EDGAR S-1 filing, press release
signals.sample_hook: Pre-IPO companies need to demonstrate AI governance maturity to investors and auditors. Getting that infrastructure in place before the roadshow matters.

signals.name: Funding Round (Series C+)
signals.description: Company raises a significant funding round (Series C or later), providing budget for infrastructure investment including AI governance.
signals.detection_method: Crunchbase, press release, SEC filing
signals.sample_hook: Post-raise companies scale fast. AI governance usually lags behind deployment by 6 months. Getting ahead of that gap is worth a conversation.

signals.name: Geographic Expansion (Multi-Region)
signals.description: Company expanding into new geographic regions, creating data residency and regulatory compliance requirements for AI systems.
signals.detection_method: Press release, job postings in new locations, regulatory filings
signals.sample_hook: Expanding into [region] means your AI systems need to comply with local regulations. Different rules, same governance platform.

signals.name: Corporate Restructuring / Reorg
signals.description: Major organizational restructuring that changes reporting lines for security and technology teams.
signals.detection_method: Press release, SEC filing (8-K), news
signals.sample_hook: Restructuring is the right time to consolidate AI governance under one platform. New org charts create new decision-makers.

signals.name: Regulatory Settlement / Fine
signals.description: Company settles with regulators or pays a fine related to data handling, privacy, cybersecurity, or technology risk.
signals.detection_method: Regulatory enforcement databases, news, SEC filings
signals.sample_hook: Regulatory settlements create urgency and budget. Companies in your position typically prioritize governance infrastructure to prevent repeat findings.

signals.name: Digital Transformation Initiative
signals.description: Company announces a named digital transformation program with executive sponsorship and dedicated budget.
signals.detection_method: Press release, annual report, CEO letter to shareholders
signals.sample_hook: Digital transformation programs that include AI need governance baked in from the start, not bolted on after the first audit finding.

signals.name: New AI-Powered Business Line / Product
signals.description: Company launches a new business line or product that relies on AI/ML, creating production governance requirements.
signals.detection_method: Press release, product launch announcement
signals.sample_hook: Launching an AI-powered product means the governance question goes from internal-only to customer-facing. Different stakes, different requirements.

categories.name: Industry Compliance Triggers
categories.description: External regulatory and compliance events that force companies to act on AI governance regardless of internal priorities.

signals.name: New AI Regulation Enacted (Sector-Specific)
signals.description: A new AI-specific regulation or amendment is enacted that directly affects companies in a specific sector.
signals.detection_method: Federal Register, state legislature trackers, regulatory agency announcements
signals.sample_hook: New regulation creates a compliance deadline. Companies that build governance infrastructure early avoid the rush.

signals.name: Enforcement Action Against Industry Peer
signals.description: A regulatory enforcement action, fine, or consent order against a peer company in the same industry for AI/technology/data issues.
signals.detection_method: Regulatory enforcement databases, news monitoring
signals.sample_hook: When [peer company] got hit with enforcement action for [issue], every company in the space took notice. The question: are you ahead of the curve or behind it?

signals.name: Audit Finding on Technology Controls
signals.description: Company's internal or external audit produces findings related to technology controls, data governance, or model risk management.
signals.detection_method: Annual report audit opinion, proxy statement disclosures
signals.sample_hook: Audit findings on technology controls create a remediation timeline. AI governance infrastructure satisfies the finding and prevents the next one.

signals.name: Data Breach Disclosed
signals.description: Company discloses a data breach, security incident, or unauthorized access event, creating urgency for better security controls including AI systems.
signals.detection_method: HHS breach portal, state AG notifications, SEC 8-K filings, news
signals.sample_hook: Post-breach, companies invest in controls they should have had. AI governance is increasingly one of them.

signals.name: Industry Guidance Updated (NIST, ISO, etc.)
signals.description: Major standards body (NIST, ISO, IEEE) updates AI governance or risk management guidance that companies in regulated industries must adopt.
signals.detection_method: Standards body publication trackers, industry association alerts
signals.sample_hook: NIST updated their AI risk management framework. Your examiners will start asking about it. Better to have the answer ready.

signals.name: Third-Party AI Vendor Risk Event
signals.description: A major AI vendor (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) experiences a security incident, policy change, or reliability event that impacts enterprise customers.
signals.detection_method: News monitoring, vendor status pages, industry alerts
signals.sample_hook: When your primary AI vendor has an incident, multi-model governance lets you failover instantly. Single-vendor dependency is the risk most companies don't price in.

signals.name: Congressional/Parliamentary Hearing on AI
signals.description: Sector-relevant Congressional hearing or parliamentary inquiry on AI governance, creating anticipation of future regulation.
signals.detection_method: Congressional record, committee hearing schedules
signals.sample_hook: Congress is asking questions about AI governance in [sector]. The regulation is coming. Companies that build the infrastructure now won't be scrambling later.

signals.name: Regulator Self-Assessment Deadline
signals.description: Supervisory letter or bulletin sets a deadline for submitting AI risk self-assessments or model inventories.
signals.detection_method: Regulator bulletins, supervisory letters, industry association compliance alerts
signals.sample_hook: When regulators demand an AI self-assessment by a specific date, teams need templates fast—we ship them pre-filled with your inventory.

categories.name: Community & Social Intent
categories.description: Person-level public intent: engaging with competitor content on LinkedIn, or asking buyer questions on Reddit. Strongest when stacked with an account-level signal from categories 1-8.

signals.name: Commented on a Competitor Post
signals.description: Person commented on a tracked competitor's LinkedIn company or exec post.
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/competitor-engagers (Apify harvestapi post + comment actors)
signals.sample_hook: Saw you weighing in on the conversation about how teams are handling this. Curious what you're running today.

signals.name: Engaged With Two or More Competitors
signals.description: Same person commented on posts from two or more tracked competitors inside the decay window. Reads as active category research.
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/competitor-engagers score step
signals.sample_hook: Looks like you've been comparing a few approaches lately. Happy to share what we see separating the ones that stick.

signals.name: Reddit Vendor Comparison
signals.description: Thread or comment comparing named vendors in the category (X vs Y).
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/reddit-signals classify = comparison
signals.sample_hook: Teams comparing these two usually get stuck on the same question. Here's how we'd answer it.

signals.name: Reddit Recommendation Ask
signals.description: Buyer asking which tool to pick, or for an alternative to a named vendor.
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/reddit-signals classify = recommendation
signals.sample_hook: If you're still shortlisting, here's the checklist buyers in your spot tell us they wish they had.

signals.name: Reddit Vendor Pain
signals.description: Complaint about price, complexity or limits of a named vendor or the category.
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/reddit-signals classify = pain
signals.sample_hook: That pricing jump is the most common reason teams start looking. Here's what switching actually took for one of them.

signals.name: Reddit Category Question
signals.description: General question about the category with no vendor named. Content signal more than an outreach trigger.
signals.detection_method: core/scripts/reddit-signals classify = question
signals.sample_hook: Use as content and language input; rarely a direct outreach trigger.

combination_rules.name: Cross-Category Signal Stacking
combination_rules.description: Two or more medium-strength signals from different categories elevate to high-confidence outreach.
combination_rules.example: Earnings call AI discussion + MLOps hiring surge = confirmed AI scale-up with governance gap

combination_rules.name: Hiring + AI Investment (30-day window)
combination_rules.description: AI governance/security hiring combined with AI budget announcement within 30 days indicates active buildout.
combination_rules.example: AI governance role posted + AI budget announced = they're building the team AND the budget exists

combination_rules.name: Leadership Change + Technology Shift
combination_rules.description: New technology/security leader combined with a technology platform change creates a natural displacement opportunity.
combination_rules.example: New CISO + security stack overhaul = new leader rebuilding the stack, perfect time to enter

combination_rules.name: Regulatory Filing + Compliance Trigger
combination_rules.description: Company's own regulatory disclosure combined with an external compliance trigger confirms governance pain is real and acknowledged.
combination_rules.example: 10-K AI risk factor + NIST framework update = company acknowledged the risk AND regulators are tightening

combination_rules.name: Triple Signal (Any Strength)
combination_rules.description: Three or more signals of any strength from at least two categories indicate enterprise-grade opportunity.
combination_rules.example: SOC hiring + cloud migration + data breach at peer = multi-signal convergence

combination_rules.name: Corporate Event + Hiring Surge
combination_rules.description: Major corporate event (M&A, funding, expansion) combined with aggressive hiring indicates rapid growth with governance lag.
combination_rules.example: M&A announcement + 5 AI engineering roles posted = integrating new AI assets fast, governance gap is real

combination_rules.name: Competitive Signal + Leadership Change
combination_rules.description: Competitive displacement signal combined with new leadership creates the highest-probability switch opportunity.
combination_rules.example: Negative vendor review + new CISO = new leader actively looking for alternatives

combination_rules.name: Data Breach + AI Investment
combination_rules.description: Company that experienced a breach and is simultaneously investing in AI creates extreme urgency for governance.
combination_rules.example: Data breach + GenAI rollout = security incident + expanding AI attack surface = must-have governance

combination_rules.name: Person Intent + Account Signal
combination_rules.description: A community-intent signal on a person at an account that already carries a medium or high signal from categories 1-8.
combination_rules.example: VP Security comments on two competitor posts the same month their company files a 10-K AI risk factor
